models.help.quantize.title: Weight precision
models.help.quantize.tip: 4 or 6 bits are almost always enough; switch to bf16 if your memory allows it and you want the most detail.
models.help.variant.title: Quantization
models.help.variant.body: A more or less compressed version of the same model. GGUF formats (Q4_K_M, Q5_K_M, Q8_0…) give the number of bits per weight: Q4 ≈ 4 bits (light, slight loss), Q5/Q6 (compromise), Q8 ≈ 8 bits (nearly lossless, twice as heavy as Q4), bf16/f16 (no compression, the heaviest). “K_M” means a finer compression that better preserves the sensitive layers. Downloading a version does not delete the others already installed: you can keep several, the setting only picks which one is used to generate. For locally quantized MLX models, quantization happens once, at install time (never redone on every load); the full unquantized copy, downloaded once to produce these versions, can then be freed from the model's card.
models.help.variant.tip: with limited memory, take Q4_K_M; as soon as the machine allows it, Q8_0 gives a more faithful result.
models.help.seconds.title: Maximum clip length
models.help.seconds.body: Length of the video. The model computes a number of frames in steps (n × step + 1): the displayed length is rounded to the closest real value. The longer the clip, the more memory and time explode: doubling the length more than doubles the wait, and the coherence of the motion weakens.
models.help.seconds.tip: start with short clips (2 to 4 s) to validate the idea.
models.help.resolution.title: Available definitions
models.help.resolution.body: Size of the image in pixels (480p, 720p…). This is the most expensive setting: 720p needs ~2.25 times more computing than 480p. Models are trained at certain native sizes; below them quality collapses (especially with Wan), and above them coherence may degrade.
models.help.resolution.tip: validate in 480p, then redo in 720p with the same seed if you like the result.
models.help.englishOnly.title: Prompt in English
models.help.englishOnly.body: This model was mostly trained on English descriptions: a prompt in French is often misunderstood. Write or have your prompt translated before generating.
models.help.audioOut.title: Soundtrack
models.help.audioOut.body: This model also generates a sound synchronized with the picture (ambience, sound effects, sometimes speech). Describe what should be heard in the prompt to steer it.
models.help.license.title: License
models.help.license.body: This model imposes usage restrictions. Check that they apply to your situation before generating or publishing videos.

models.hub.help.llm: Language models in GGUF format (text generation, vision) that llama.cpp can run.
models.help.llmVision.title: Vision
models.help.llmVision.body: The model reads the images you attach to a message (screenshots, photos, diagrams) through an extra file, the multimodal projector, downloaded with it.
models.help.llmTools.title: Tools
models.help.llmTools.body: The model can ask for a function to be run (a web search, for instance) and then use the result. Required for the chat's web search.
models.help.llmReasoning.title: Thinking
models.help.llmReasoning.body: The model thinks before answering: answers are better on hard questions but take longer to start. Its thinking is shown in a collapsible block.
models.help.llmMoe.title: Mixture of experts (MoE)
models.help.llmMoe.body: The model only activates part of its parameters for each word: it answers almost as fast as a small model but takes the memory of the big one.
models.help.llmParams.title: Parameters
models.help.llmParams.body: Number of parameters in billions. The bigger, the more capable, heavier and slower the model.
models.help.llmContext.title: Maximum context
models.help.llmContext.body: How much text (in thousands of tokens) the model can keep in mind: conversation, attached documents. The chat opens with a shorter context; enlarging it needs more memory.
models.hub.placeholder.ocr: e.g. glm ocr, paddleocr, dots ocr…
models.hub.help.ocr: Vision models in GGUF format made to read the text of images and documents, which llama.cpp can run.
